definitions.explanation: An orange fruit native to East Asia, eaten fresh when ripe or dried. Persimmons are a symbol of autumn in Japan.

examples.english: The persimmons in the garden are starting to ripen.

There is a large persimmon tree at my grandmother's house in the countryside.

notes:
{柿|かき} refers to persimmons.

Types:
- ⟦{甘柿|あまがき}→甘柿：30095_amagaki⟧ (sweet persimmon - can be eaten fresh)
- ⟦{渋柿|しぶがき}→渋柿：27688_shibugaki⟧ (astringent persimmon - must be dried or processed)
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧ (dried persimmon)

Common expressions:
- {柿|かき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{種|たね}→種：02157_tane⟧ (persimmon seed; also a type of rice cracker)
- {柿|かき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{赤|あか}く→赤い：00585_akai⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{青|あお}く→青い：00586_aoi⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (when persimmons turn red, doctors turn pale - persimmons are healthy)

Cultural note:
Persimmon trees are common in Japanese gardens and countryside. The orange persimmons hanging from bare branches are an iconic autumn scene. ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧ (dried persimmons) are made by peeling and hanging persimmons to dry, transforming astringent persimmons into a sweet treat. The famous haiku by Masaoka Shiki mentions persimmons: 「{柿|かき}⟦{食|く}えば→食う：02657_kuu⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}る→鳴る：01143_naru⟧⟦なり→なり：noentry⟧⟦{法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ}→法隆寺：noentry⟧」
